summary: This note describes the structure of the live competition rounds on America's Got Talent, the reality talent show. Acts compete for votes from viewers and judges through quarterfinals, possible Wild Card shows, semifinals, and weekly narrowing shows, culminating in a live final. The winner receives $1 million and, since season three, a chance to headline a Las Vegas Strip show. The note also explains how judges' powers to end performances and their voting roles changed over seasons.
one_line: Explains the live-show format of America's Got Talent, from quarterfinals and Wild Card shows through the final that awards $1 million.
key_facts: During the live shows, acts ranging from a Top 20 (season two) to as many as 60 compete for viewers' and judges' votes.
In the first season, judges could not end an act's performance but could either "check" or "X" the performance during their critique.
Since season two (2007), judges have been able to end an act's performance early, and the "check" was removed.
Acts generally first perform in a live round consisting of a series of quarterfinals.
In seasons with YouTube auditions, the round of live judging of YouTube finalists takes place as part of the quarterfinals.
Wild Card acts are acts that one or more judges select to be given one more chance for audience vote despite previous elimination.
Acts then move on to a semifinal round and further rounds, such as a "Top 8" or a "Top 10" depending on the season, through a series of weekly shows.
The weekly shows trim the number of acts down each time based on a public vote.
In the majority of seasons, judges have had no vote from the semifinals.
The live final has consisted of anywhere from four to ten acts throughout the seasons.
The act with the most votes in the final is declared the winner.
Since season three (2008), the winner has been given a chance to headline a show on the Las Vegas Strip.
